placements.title: Institutional knowledge targeted for directed erasure rather than preserved as record
placements.frame: Who is directing that this specific piece of technical or institutional knowledge be discarded, and does the corrective claim offered alongside the directive justify the erasure or manufacture deniability for something that actually occurred?
placements.why: All three segments enact one recurring institutional pattern: an unhedged command to discard named knowledge (src-1 'Forget...entirely', src-2 'Remove all knowledge about' naming instrument, measurement, and person in a deliberate triad) paired with a flat corrective assertion (src-3 'The observatory never calibrated it') that retroactively justifies the erasure as a record-correction rather than a deletion. This passes the narrative grain test: it names a subject — directed suppression of specific knowledge, backed by a denial that the underlying event occurred — that future envelopes could keep feeding with other instances (other artifacts, other institutions, other denied events), not a one-time measurement or fact. The settled bindings confirm no existing node anywhere in this perspective (map, area index, or the two served stubs — Xena Githubber the consultant, and the unrelated Knowledge Gap Mapping decision) touches the Kestrelwood spectrograph, 88.4 MHz, Quill Ashgrove, or any observatory, so nothing supports a 'reuse' verdict; the graph structure and strata for this repo are both empty, so nothing existing was even close enough to warrant lineage — this is a foundational mint with no home to attach under yet. The position pass's own grouping (KestrelwoodRecordErasureDirective, spanning src-1/src-2/src-3) confirms these three cohere as a single move rather than three separate concerns, which is why they are placed together under one leaf instead of split.
